preconditions.description: n is the number of crimes (0 ≤ n ≤ 10¹⁸) and c is the number of conditions (0 ≤ c ≤ 1000).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= m <= 123 for (t, m) in conditions)
preconditions.description: Each condition's multiplicity m is a positive integer (1 ≤ m ≤ 123).
There are at most 26 distinct crime types (capital Latin letters).

preconditions.expression: all('A' <= t <= 'Z' for (t, m) in conditions)
preconditions.description: Each crime type t is a capital Latin letter (A-Z).

preconditions.expression: product := 1; all(product * m <= 123 for (t, m) in conditions)
preconditions.description: The product of all multiplicities does not exceed 123.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer modulo 12345.

postconditions.expression: conditions := [tuple(line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2:]] if c > 0 else []; crime_types := {t for (t, m) in conditions}
postconditions.description: Parse input into conditions (crime type and multiplicity) and extract unique crime types.

postconditions.expression: crime_multiplicities := {t: [int(m) for m in ms] for t, ms in groupby(sorted(conditions, key=lambda x: x[0]), key=lambda x: x[0])}
postconditions.description: Group multiplicities by crime type, allowing multiple conditions per crime.

postconditions.expression: is_safe := lambda t, k: k == 0 or any(k % m == 0 for m in crime_multiplicities.get(t, []))
postconditions.description: A crime t with count k is safe if k=0 or k is a multiple of at least one of its multiplicities.

postconditions.expression: dp := [0] * (n + 1); dp[0] = 1; crime_counts := {t: 0 for t in crime_types}
postconditions.description: Dynamic programming array initialized for counting sequences, with dp[0] = 1 (empty sequence).

postconditions.expression: for i in range(1, n + 1): dp[i] = sum(dp[i - k] for t in crime_types for k in range(1, i + 1) if is_safe(t, k))
postconditions.description: For each length i, sum valid sequences by appending a safe crime (count k) to sequences of length i-k.
The result is the count of valid sequences of length n modulo 12345.
